title: The Lantern Marches
purpose: Player-facing exploration atlas for choosing routes between a fortified city, wild country and uncanny landmarks. Not a token-scale battlemap.

inspiration.premise: A river kingdom survives under an ancient astronomical citadel, while three glass monoliths awaken on its eastern frontier.

references.source: Visual observations from the user-provided regional-map screenshot; image bytes are not bundled.
use_traits: pictorial mountains and buildings within overhead geography
ignore_traits: original place names and exact geography

style.medium: Fine ink-and-watercolor fantasy cartography with carefully drawn miniature architecture.
style.linework: Thin charcoal contours; finer hatching inside landforms; distinct silhouettes without heavy comic outlines.
style.surface_texture: Subtle matte paper tooth, not distressed parchment stains. Low-contrast texture in open land and water.
style.lighting: Soft overcast daylight with light coming from upper left; gentle relief shading, no cast shadows hiding paths.

environment.terrain_summary: A broad south-draining valley between a wooded western slope and a steep eastern plateau. Northern mountains frame the citadel; the southern river mouth opens to the sea.
exceptions: The three glass spires are supernatural constructions; their shapes need not follow natural geology. Rivers and travel routes otherwise follow plausible terrain.

citadel.name: Crown of Tides
citadel.appearance: A compact limestone city on a low escarpment, encircled by terraced walls and crowned by a single enormous tilted bronze astronomical ring. The ring is the unique regional silhouette.
must_show: one oversized bronze ring, not a skull

western_wood.name: The Pale Boughs
western_wood.appearance: A dense wedge of white-barked forest with a few leaning old trunks and small clearings, drawn as coherent wooded masses rather than evenly scattered tree icons.
western_wood.gameplay_role: A slower wilderness route on the west side of the valley

northern_ridge.name: The Rimeback
northern_ridge.appearance: An irregular chain of pale angular peaks, taller to the northeast, lower at the central pass.

glass_spires.name: The Three Listeners
glass_spires.appearance: Exactly three tall, narrow smoky-glass monoliths rise from a flat basalt shelf. One is visibly tilted, one split at its top, and one intact. Space them so they remain individually countable.
must_show: a visible ascending trail from the west
glass_spires.gameplay_role: Eastern exploration objective visible from far away

copper_marsh.name: The Ember Reeds
copper_marsh.appearance: A low copper-and-rust reed marsh with dark pools and a few raised hummocks, providing the sole warm color mass in the lower-right region.
copper_marsh.gameplay_role: A hazardous optional detour, not a wall of vegetation

river.name: The Lowwater
river.appearance: A connected slate-blue river descending from below the citadel through the valley and into a small southern delta. Keep upstream narrower and downstream broader.
river.gameplay_role: Divides travel choices and establishes the valley direction

stone_bridge.name: The Last Arch
stone_bridge.appearance: A single worn pale-stone arch spanning the narrow river, with visibly connected approaches on both banks.
must_show: the river remains visible below the arch

south_port.name: Lantern Quay
south_port.appearance: A small fishing and caravan port on the western river mouth, with clustered low roofs, two short jetties and a warm beacon tower.

watchtower.name: The Leaning Watch
watchtower.appearance: One roofless square watchtower leaning slightly on a low grassy knoll. The missing upper corner makes it recognizable at small scale.

south_sea.name: The Somber Reach
south_sea.appearance: A calm strip of blue-gray coastal water at the lower edge; the Lowwater visibly empties here.

sealed_observatory.name: The Sealed Observatory
sealed_observatory.appearance: A small concealed observatory chamber within the citadel.
sealed_observatory.gm_notes: The green dial unlocks the room at midnight. Do not include the chamber, its marker or this fact in a player-facing image.

pilgrim_road.appearance: A pale packed-earth road, clearly differentiated from the blue river; it crosses only at the stone bridge.

spire_ascent.appearance: A narrow switchback ascent with a believable ramp onto the basalt shelf.

western_branch.appearance: A secondary dirt trail across open grass with occasional broken boundary stones.

marsh_detour.appearance: A narrow raised path ending at the marsh edge; do not conceal its entrance.

relationships.detail: The city sits upstream above the river crossing.
The spires occupy the eastern plateau, not the western forest.
Keep the watchtower on the same western side as the port approach.
The arch crosses the actual river, not a neighboring dry channel.
The river outlet meets the coastal water without a strip of land blocking it.
This relationship is private and absent from player art.

affordances: a fast main road versus optional rough detours
a high eastern landmark visible from lower terrain
must_preserve: distinct silhouettes for city, spires and watchtower
broad quiet areas for reading terrain

annotations.typography: Small-cap serif geographic labels, dark charcoal, restrained tracking; add outside the image generator.

clear_zones.purpose: low-detail ground for the citadel label

must_include: a readable network of public travel routes
must_avoid: borrowed place names from the reference
production.revision_notes: Original demonstration setting. The supplied screenshot informed broad visual traits, not copied names or geography.
